title: ergostat model
description: An ergostat.yaml file (or a file it includes). See docs/SPEC.md.

purpose.description: What the whole model is for (main file only): a goal in no system that says what it is for is traced to it (SPEC section 4a).

budget.description: The day's AI budget (SPEC 9.9): no charged run starts unless daily, less what runs spent over the last day and what runs in flight reserved, covers max-cost. Main file only.

daily.description: US dollars over the trailing 24 hours

max-cost.description: dollars a charged run reserves before it starts (at most daily); not a cap on what it spends

operating.description: The operating state's settings (SPEC 12k): away-after, how long with no event from the owner before they read as away (default 2h, from 5m to 7d). Main file only.

dashboards.description: Shared, named dashboards (SPEC section 4f); in a file whose defaults: set a system, each is named SYSTEM.NAME.

runs.description: How a machine block's run is held (SPEC 9.1). Main file or ergostat.local.yaml only.

outlive_engine.description: true: each run is kept by a detached keeper and writes its own journal, so stopping ergostat (or a crash) leaves it going; default false

variables.description: The old name of auxiliaries: (still read, with a finding)

claims.description: The checks the project declares for its blocks' claims (SPEC §12g): tests, the project's test command; any other name, a kind of claim of its own

messages.description: How the owner's messages are routed to the work in flight, and what a message about finished work does (SPEC §12h)

classifier.description: A machine block (an ai block on a cheap model) that routes a message no id or name in it routes; else ergostat's stand-in

finished.description: A message about finished work: a new item linked to it, the item moved back, or left to the owner

follow-up.description: The kind of item a follow-up is made as (default: the finished item's own)

reopen-to.description: By kind, the state reopening moves an item back to (default: its first)

done.description: By kind, the states an item is finished in (default: inferred from the record)

storage.description: Where the record is kept: the backends, raw readings and their tiers, item rollup (SPEC §4b)

items.description: The item index (SPEC §4b): only open items are kept folded in memory

idle.description: An item with no event for this long is read from the index, not kept folded in memory (default 1d)

logs.description: Caps on the logs that would otherwise grow without limit (SPEC §4b)

block.description: A block's log past this is cut to its last fifth (default 5MB)

run.description: run.log past this is moved to run.log.1 (default 5MB)

threads.description: threads.txt past this is cut to its last fifth (default 1MB)

transcripts.description: A transcript unchanged this long is forgotten (default 30d)

web.description: The page's public names and the Cloudflare Access login in front of them (SPEC §4d); main file only

names.description: The public host names the page answers to

open.description: The names are public and read only, with no login (in place of access)

intake.description: What may push events to the running ergostat (POST /api/events, /api/hooks/NAME): who besides this machine, where the page listens, and each webhook's mapping (docs/proposals/latency.md)

allow.description: Addresses or networks that may push besides this machine

bind.description: The address the page listens on (default 127.0.0.1)

contexts.description: Named, versioned projection recipes for sessions' starting contexts (SPEC §12i)

actions.description: The outward acts AI sessions may ask for, each a command run only as its gate says (SPEC §12k)

workspaces.description: Pools of workspaces (git worktrees) AI blocks' sessions work in, one per item (SPEC §12k)

daemons.description: Long-lived runners several blocks and sensors may share (SPEC §9.7)

operating.description: Operating states: entered by the owner or a goal's trip, capping the pool of every block that takes items (SPEC §9.5)

leases.description: Each tier's lease terms, over the defaults (SPEC §9.5)

uses.description: Instances of templates (SPEC §2a): each expands into ordinary parts named for it, and is a system of its own

within.description: the system it is part of

remotes.description: Systems other ergostats run, read here (SPEC §4c): each brings in the remote's model as an external subsystem whose parts are named for it

token-file.description: the file holding the token the remote made for this model

library.description: Folders of the owner's own templates (main file only; SPEC §2a)

libraries.description: Libraries fetched by git URL into .libraries/NAME, pinned in libraries.lock (main file only, at most 16; SPEC §2a). The loader's allowlists are stricter than these patterns.

dashboard.description: A shared, named dashboard (SPEC section 4f): one window for all its panels; display only.

panel.description: One panel: its kind, its words, and exactly the parameters its endpoint takes (SPEC section 4f).

ref.description: kind.name or kind.name.port, e.g. stock.inbox, goal.inbox-short.error, block.decide.urgent, flow.processed

push.description: Its daemon sends its readings by itself: none asked for

averages.description: On a flow's run, query or manual sensor: its reading is the average rate over this window before it

changes.description: On a flow: its rate from its stock's own successive readings

builtin.description: One of ergostat's built-in measures: the model's own quality (SPEC §12e, §12f), how far blocks' claims hold (SPEC §12g), how the owner's messages reach the work (SPEC §12h), or how the work a recipe started turned out (SPEC §12i)

observe.description: Estimated between readings, its staleness watched (SPEC section 9.6)

cumulative.description: A running total that by its nature never drains (spent so far): no outflow is missing (SPEC section 5)

rate-unit.description: How the rates of its flows are shown, where a flow says none (display only: rates are kept per hour)

two-way.description: It may run either way (a biflow): a block may move it by a negative amount

rate-unit.description: How the rate is shown (display only: rates are kept per hour)

per.description: Held by each item (item) or each group of items by a field (a relation such as parent), of a stock counted from items

process.description: The loop's process, from what its controller moves to what the goal holds: first order with dead time, or an integrator (SPEC §8, §12c)

gain.description: A proportional block's gain; on a machine block, its law's gain (passed in its params)

identify.description: An external block's law, identified from the record of what it reads and what it sets (SPEC §12d)

law.description: An external block's known law, declared with identify: (SPEC §12d, Known laws): kubernetes-hpa or alert-rule and its parameters

integral-time.description: A machine block's integral time, when its law is PI (passed in its params)

accept.description: A judge's policy: who writes a change it passed (owner, the default, or auto), for every kind or by kind

threshold.description: A judge's least fall in scaled error that counts, in every window

hold-out.description: A judge's record after a change that it is judged on

warm-up.description: A judge's replay of each window starts this long before it (default 6h)

windows.description: A judge's split of the record held out: [1, 2, 4], whole, halves, quarters

context.description: An ai block: the recipe its runs start from (contexts:), and the item a run works on when its command names none

review.description: A machine block: who reviews its work, and how deeply, by a measure (its trust); the first rule that holds decides

when.description: a built-in measure, a comparison and a number; contradicted (and the other trust counts) alone is the block's own trust
a built-in measure, a comparison and a number; contradicted (and the other trust counts) alone is the block's own trust

judge.description: A judge's job: model (changes to the model, SPEC §12e, the default) or intent (finished work held to what the owner meant, SPEC §12i)

kinds.description: An intent judge's: the item kinds it judges, each the state it is judged in (at:) and more

max-cost.description: An intent judge on a model: dollars a verdict, at most

held.description: An intent judge's: what a verdict that the work is not done as meant does

within.description: An intent judge's: work that entered its judged state longer ago is not judged late

workdir.description: An ai block: the folder its session works in (SPEC §12k)

workspace.description: An ai block: the pool its session takes a workspace from, per item (SPEC §12k)

read.description: An ai block: more folders its session may read

tools.description: An ai block: the Claude Code tools its session may use (gated: SPEC §12k)

actions.description: An ai block: the gated actions its session may ask for

read-only.description: A program or ai block: its program changes nothing outside, so a repair's fix to it is re-run for real on the input that failed, in the sandbox (SPEC §12r)

network.description: A read-only block: the hosts a re-run of a repair's fix may reach, through the sandbox's proxy, for GET and HEAD only (SPEC §12r)

pool.description: The most runs of a block that takes items at once: a number, or a stock's level read at each dispatch, held within 0 and most

now.description: The stock whose level is the pool now (it must have a sensor)

most.description: The hard ceiling: never more at once, whatever the stock reads

runs-on.description: A program block: the compute pool its runs are for (a name under compute:), or local (here, as with none). Refused on an ai, person or daemon's block, on a command that calls ergostat, and for a pool whose blocks are in two shards (SPEC §12k)

token-file.description: an ergostat source (SPEC §4c): the file holding its token

show.description: The measures its box shows: stock, flow or auxiliary references

fold.description: How each field folds the plain data its events carry: replace (the default), append (to a list), sum, min, max, union (a set, kept as a sorted list), merge (a deep merge of objects), first (keep the first value, relation (a set of item ids: ids added, or {set, add, remove}))

about.description: The field that names the parts of the model each item is about (goal.x, stock.y, flow.z, auxiliary.w, block.v), folded by replace (SPEC section 5a, About). explain, check and status point at the open items about a part

attention.description: The field whose words, on the latest item of the kind that has them (by its latest event), are shown on the attention list: a finding that needs the owner, said where it is seen (SPEC section 5a)

title.description: The default dashboard's row for it

stages.description: The stage names its histograms are labelled by (any other: other)

waiting.description: The line of work it takes from: a kind, its state, the fields it is taken in order of

pipeline.description: Its items record named stages, folded into stages by merge (SPEC section 5a, Stages)

final.description: States no event moves an item out of: a later move is ignored and said (SPEC section 5a)

relations.description: Its typed relations to other items (SPEC section 5a, Relations): each a field holding the ids it names, folded as a set. A kind, a list of kinds, or {kind, precedence, inverse, group}. blocked_by, after and depends_on are precedence (the item is ready once each item it names is finished); parent is a group. Never enforced

precedence.description: Its targets come first: the item is ready once each is finished

inverse.description: The other direction's name, derived (blocks, children)

group.description: A parent: the Graph view hangs its children off it

starts_at.description: A precedence relation's target states (neither finished nor paused) at which it no longer blocks: the item is unblocked, and takes: {unblocked: true} may take it. The critical path and the schedule stay finish-to-start

done_when.description: A group's: for a finished state of the item's, the fields it counts as done work in ({closed: {end: done}}); an item in that state not matching them leaves its group's total in the progress per group

join.description: Its children move it on (SPEC section 5a, Join): a rule, or a list of them

exogenous.description: An input from outside the model: nothing in it drives it

auxiliary.description: A quantity without memory: determined at each moment by others (SPEC section 7a)

driven_by.description: What it follows: flow., stock. or auxiliary. references, each optionally signed (+ rises with it, - falls; unsigned: not known); an entry may be written out as {cause, instant, description, inferred}: instant says the dependence is immediate (SPEC section 7); inferred, that ergostat added the link (SPEC section 12e)

instant.description: The effect follows the cause in the same moment, with no stock between (silences rate-driven-by-rate)

equation.description: Its rate per hour (a flow) or its value (an auxiliary), as an equation of parameters (bare names) and parts (stock.x, flow.x, auxiliary.x): + - * / ^, MIN, MAX, ABS, EXP, LN, SQRT, DELAY1, DELAY3, SMOOTH, SMOOTH3, and a lookup parameter called like a function. Subtraction is written with spaces (a - b): names have hyphens (SPEC §7b)

parameter.description: A number an equation names: its value (a number, or a duration read in hours), its unit, and whether to estimate it from the record; or a lookup's table. A bare number is short for value:

value.description: A number, or a duration (40s, 2h) read in hours

estimate.description: Fit it from the record: estimates are kept apart, and become the value only when a proposal is accepted

range.description: What it might be, [low, high] (numbers, or durations read in hours): sensitivity analysis samples it uniformly there

table.description: A lookup's points: a map x: y or a list of [x, y]

run.description: The command; exit 0 means what was claimed holds

in.description: Where it runs, from the model's folder (and the repository a claim's commit is taken from)

says.description: A pattern over what a claim says that makes it this kind

context_budget.description: characters (6000) or tokens (1500t, four characters a token)

context_part.description: One part of a recipe: its kind alone, or its kind with its keys

decisions.description: the owner's confirmed decisions, most relevant to scope first

corrections.description: what the owner corrected before, for this kind of work

from.description: record (the default), or transcript files or folders

owner-words.description: the owner's messages, verbatim, most relevant to the topic, the item or its parts first

item-history.description: the item's fields and history, and the key turns of the sessions that worked on it

state.description: what moved on the main branch, what is running, the open findings on the item's parts

session.description: a session's turns: all, the last N, or those matching a pattern (of: item, a session item, or a transcript file)

model.description: the item's parts in the model, and their goals

version.description: raised when the recipe changes; recorded with every use

outcome.description: the states of the item worked on that count as the work's success or failure

context.description: A projection recipe (SPEC §12i): parts rendered in order, each within its budget, into a starting context

inferred.description: Added by ergostat (SPEC section 12e): the model change that added it, ergostat.model-change/<id>, or true where that is not known. It stays when the owner accepts or edits the part; taking the key away makes it declared

run.description: The command template: {name} is one of its args, or ergostat's own ({item}, {branch}, {workdir}, {block}, {run}), each shell-quoted

gate.description: auto: run at once; approve: held until the owner approves; deny: never run (default approve); or a map by operating state, a cell of which may be {reshape: ACTION}: that smaller action asked for at once, this one held

class.description: The class it is counted in (default: its name)

args.description: What the session gives: each argument's name and what it is

wait.description: How long a session waits for the owner before going on (default 5m)

in.description: Where it runs, from the model's folder (default: the session's folder)

type.description: How a workspace is made: a git worktree of repo

repo.description: The repository, from the model's folder or a whole path

pool.description: Where its workspaces are made (default: workspaces/NAME in the state directory)

branch.description: The item's branch, a template of its fields: {kind}/{id}-{slug}

base.description: The ref a new branch is made from (default HEAD)

daemon.description: A long-lived process blocks' runs and sensors' readings are handed to as JSON lines (SPEC §9.7)

warm.description: The program keeps no state between runs: concurrency processes, one run each at a time, its CPU charged to the run

recycle.description: With warm: the most runs one process serves

daemon_use.description: A map of its own, or the name of one under daemons:

lease_terms.description: A lease's terms (SPEC §9.5): how long a run may be silent before its lease expires, and the counted attempts before the item is a dead letter

takes.description: The items a block works (SPEC §9.5): one run per item of the kind that reaches a state in at:, each leasing its item

unblocked.description: Only items whose precedence relations name only finished items, the critical first (SPEC section 5a, Relations)

faults.description: The queue's shared environment (SPEC section 9.5): while healthy reads unhealthy or unknown the block takes nothing new, and a run failing through the outage is given back uncounted; hold-by: item fields whose values, failing together, are held each on its own

hold-by.description: An item field, or a list of 1 to 8: a value whose items fail together (3 in a row, of 2 items or more, within 10 minutes) is held, probed after a back-off, and released by a success

healthy.description: A sensor (sensor.NAME, the part it reads), a stock, flow or auxiliary (healthy above 0), a goal (healthy while it holds) or a block's output

join.description: To to: once all (or any) of the items naming it by the relation children: are in those states; only forward

trigger.description: What starts a program or ai block (SPEC section 9.3, Started by an event): a run for each recorded event of these types whose data matches where:, one at a time, caused by the event; emits: the types its runs say (a loop among such blocks is refused)
